key_insight: Interfacial lattice distortion in HoFeO3–BaTiO3 nanofibers is consistent with stabilized ferroelectric domains and enhanced hybrid energy harvesting.
engineering_relevance: Lead-free oxide nanofiber heterostructures offer a route to improve mechanical-energy harvesting in flexible PDMS-encapsulated devices.
method: Fabricate HoFeO3–BaTiO3 heterostructures by alternating sol–gel electrospinning.
Probe crystal structure and interfaces using Rietveld-refined XRD, high-resolution TEM, and Raman spectroscopy.
Measure polarization switching and cyclic-impact energy harvesting against single-oxide controls.
evidence_signal: The heterostructure retained polarization comparable to BaTiO3 (16.39 vs 15.80 µC/cm² at zero field) and delivered 24.31 µW/cm³ at 4.7 MΩ, outperforming BaTiO3 and HoFeO3 controls by 2.4× and 8.7×.
watch_item: The reported output combines piezoelectric and triboelectric contributions, so their separate roles require quantification.
paper_title: Stabilization of Ferroelectric Domains via Interfacial Strain in HoFeO3- BaTiO3 Nanofiber Heterostructures for Enhanced Hybrid Energy Harvesting
